title: Nilpotent group scheme via a finite central series
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. It is nilpotent if there exist an integer $s\geq 0$ and closed normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] $G=H_0\supseteq H_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_s=1$ such that, for every $0\leq j<s$, every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, every $g\in G(A)$ and every $h\in H_j(A)$, the element $ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$ belongs to $H_{j+1}(A)$. The subgroup schemes in the series need not be smooth or connected; a zero-length series is allowed.
